questions.stem: Two DNA duplexes of equal length have melting temperatures of 85 C and 72 C. The higher Tm sample most likely has
options: a higher percentage of A-T base pairs
a higher percentage of G-C base pairs
questions.explanation: G-C pairs have three hydrogen bonds and stack more strongly, so more G-C raises Tm. More A-T lowers Tm, nicks do not raise stability, and lower salt would lower Tm by increasing phosphate repulsion.

questions.stem: Why do human chromosomes need many replication origins?
options: Eukaryotic forks are slow relative to genome size
Origins must fire many times per S phase
questions.explanation: At about 50 nt/s, a single origin could not copy hundreds of millions of base pairs in S phase, so many origins fire in parallel. Human chromosomes are linear, and origins fire once per cycle because of licensing.

questions.stem: The template strand of a gene is 3'-TACGTTAA-5'. What is the mRNA?
questions.explanation: RNA pairs antiparallel with the template and uses U for T: 5'-AUGCAAUU-3'. The first option copies the template, the second contains T, and the last is written in the wrong direction.

questions.stem: A mutant activator keeps its DNA-binding domain but lacks its activation domain. In the cell it would most likely
options: bind the enhancer but fail to stimulate transcription
questions.explanation: The DNA-binding domain still docks on the enhancer, but without the activation domain it cannot recruit coactivators. It can even compete with the normal activator.
questions.subtopic: Eukaryotic transcription factors, enhancers and silencers

questions.stem: In a Sanger reaction the ddNTP to dNTP ratio is increased tenfold. The fragments will
questions.explanation: A higher ddNTP fraction terminates chains earlier, producing shorter fragments. Lower ddNTP would give longer fragments, and termination still occurs at multiple positions.

demo_cards.front: Nucleoside versus nucleotide: what is the difference?
demo_cards.back: A nucleoside is sugar plus base. Adding one or more phosphate groups makes it a nucleotide.

demo_cards.text: A nucleotide has a {{c1::phosphate group}}, a {{c1::pentose sugar}}, and a {{c1::nitrogenous base}}.

demo_cards.stem: In a nucleotide, the nitrogenous base is attached to which sugar carbon?
demo_cards.why: The base sits on C1' through an N-glycosidic bond. C5' carries the phosphate and C3' carries the OH that accepts the next nucleotide.

demo_cards.statement: RNA is chemically less stable than DNA because of the 2' hydroxyl on ribose.
demo_cards.why: The 2' OH can attack the neighboring phosphodiester bond, so RNA hydrolyzes more easily, especially in base.
